summary: The team is pivoting its global marketing weight behind Asia Star and the new Intelligent China program, while closing out a knowledge website redesign and clearing a batch of time-sensitive follow-ups this week.
summaryDetail: The strategic center of gravity is now the China-based programs: Asia Star and Intelligent China are the top two priorities for search/AI visibility, with US partnerships (Stanford, Columbia, Berkeley) pushed to secondary and Berkeley folded into the audit phase. On that front, Joseph owes the initial target-areas/prompts list and the Asia Star participant/CRM hot-lead analysis, the team needs the SEO manager's conversion-tracking brief before auditing, and the Intelligent China webpage still needs to launch and drive traffic. The knowledge website redesign is converging on a keep-the-current-design approach with better menu categorization and Joseph's editorial-style layout to surface more articles and the BCI index banner, so Joseph's HTML file, a 30-minute feedback session, and Joker's revisions are the immediate blockers. This week also carries a cluster of high-stakes items: Ira must run the AACSB Global Impact Award application by Prof Zhu today, Jay leads the Yili Group digitalization enquiry with Cao Yi monitoring, Joseph sends updated Asia Start campaign reports to European colleagues, and Tian briefs the Asia Start photographer for the Beijing campus shoot. Looming after that are the Flow design PPT and Dean Xiang transcript reviews, the video strategy meeting with Joseph and Julie, and the Outlook lockout cleanup across devices.

decisions.text: Account lock was resolved by unlocking the backend; users must update passwords on all devices.
Remove the standalone videos section; videos will be dispersed by topic instead.
Keep the two-menu structure (Knowledge and School) at the top.
Bring the BCI index banner into the knowledge section, similar to the school homepage.
Do not add a stock-market ticker at the very top of the homepage.
Use Joseph's editorial-style layout as inspiration to display more articles, combining selected ideas with the current version.
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China as top two programs; US partnerships (Stanford, Columbia, Berkeley) secondary for now.
Consider Berkeley as a possible third priority and include it in the audit phase.
Focus initial campaign on outcomes and target audience research before expanding.
Forward the Contact Us submission to Alan and his team
